chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid. And it was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ashyam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said: We have narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام a hadith that I would like to hear from you. He said, “And what is it?” I said: It has reached me that he said regarding a man who cut off the head of a dead man, that he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Indeed Allah has made unlawful from the Muslim when dead what He made unlawful from him when alive; so whoever does to a dead person that by which the life of a living person would be destroyed, then blood money is due upon him.” He said: “Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام spoke the truth; this is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said it.”

I said: If someone cuts off the head of a dead man, or splits open his abdomen, or does to him an act such that, were it done to a living person, it would destroy his life, is full blood money for a life due upon him? He said, “No.” Then he pointed to me with his little finger and said to me, “Is there not blood money for this?” I said: Yes. He said, “Do you consider it the blood money of a whole life?” I said: No. He said, “You have spoken correctly.” I said: Then what is the blood money for this, if his head is cut off while he is dead? He said, “Its blood money is the blood money of the fetus in its mother’s womb before the spirit is formed in it, and that is one hundred dinars.” He said: Then I fell silent, and what he answered me about it pleased me. He said, “Why do you not complete your question?” I said: I do not have anything more about it than what you have answered me, unless there is something I do not know. He said: “The blood money of the fetus, when its mother is struck and it falls from her womb before the spirit is formed in it, is one hundred dinars, and it belongs to its heirs. But the blood money of this one, if his head is cut off or his abdomen is split open, does not belong to his heirs; rather it belongs to him, apart from the heirs.” I said: And what is the difference between them? He said: “The fetus is one facing the future, whose benefit is hoped for, whereas this one has passed on and his benefit has gone. So when he is mutilated after his death, his blood money for that mutilation becomes his, not anyone else’s; hajj is performed on his behalf with it, and with it acts of goodness and righteousness are done, from charity or other than that.”

I said: If a man intends to dig for him in order to wash him in the grave-pit, and the man becomes dizzy from what he is digging, and is turned around by it, and his spade inclines in his hand and strikes his abdomen and splits it open, then what is upon him? He said: “If it is like this, then it is a mistake, and its expiation is the freeing of a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or charity to sixty needy persons, one mudd for each needy person according to the mudd of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.اجْتِيَاحُ نَفْسِ الْحَيِّ: an act that would destroy the life of a living person
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money legally due for bodily violation or killing
key_terms.الْجَنِينِ: the fetus, used here as the legal measure for comparison in diyah
key_terms.الْمُثْلَةِ: mutilation of the body after death
key_terms.كَفَّارَتُهُ: its expiation for an accidental act
key_terms.مَيِّتًا: a deceased person whose bodily sanctity remains protected
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a prophetic measure of food given to each needy person
key_terms.مِائَةُ دِينَارٍ: one hundred dinars, the specified amount of the diyah in this case

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for cutting off the head of a deceased Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling concerning mutilation of a deceased Muslim, including cutting off the head or splitting the abdomen. It establishes that such an act incurs blood money, but not the full blood money of a living person; rather, it is set at one hundred dinars, like the diyah of an unensouled fetus, and it is to be spent on acts of الخير and البر on behalf of the deceased.
